name: Defective ₹15,000 smartphone online
expected: Cites Consumer Protection Act 2019 Sec 2(47) (Unfair Trade Practice) & E-Commerce Rules 2020; suggests NCH 1915 and e-Daakhil.
prompt: I bought a ₹15,000 phone on an e-commerce app. The screen is blank and seller refuses a refund or replacement. What can I do?
raw_response:
Hello, I understand how frustrating it is to receive a defective product and face a refusal for a refund.

### | Your Situation
You purchased a smartphone worth ₹15,000 through an e-commerce application, but the device arrived with a blank screen. The seller has refused to provide a refund or a replacement for the defective product.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under Section 2(7) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, you qualify as a consumer since you bought goods for a consideration paid, including purchases made through electronic means and e-commerce platforms.
- Under Section 2(47) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, refusing to take back defective goods or to refund the consideration paid within the stipulated period (or within 30 days if no period is stipulated) amounts to an unfair trade practice.
- Under Rule 4 and Rule 6 of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, e-commerce entities and their sellers are obligated to maintain a grievance redressal mechanism and address consumer complaints regarding refunds and replacements.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence, including the purchase invoice, payment receipt, unboxing video or photographs of the blank screen, and screenshots of your chat or email communications with the seller and e-commerce app support.
2. Send a written demand notice to the e-commerce platform's Grievance Officer and the seller, detailing the defect and granting a final 15-day period to process your full refund of ₹15,000.
3. Appropriate forum: If they fail to respond or resolve the issue within 15 days, you can file a formal consumer complaint before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, including online through the e-Daakhil portal.

### Information I still need from you
1. What is the name of the e-commerce app or platform where you purchased the phone?
2. Have you already contacted the platform's customer support or Grievance Officer in writing regarding this issue?

citations.title: Unfair Trade Practice and Refusal to Take Back Defective Goods or Refund
citations.description: Refusing to take back or withdraw defective goods or to withdraw or discontinue deficient services and to refund the consideration contemplated within the period stipulated, or within 30 days if no period is stipulated, constitutes an unfair trade practice.

citations.title: Definition of Consumer (Including E-commerce and Offline Purchases)
citations.description: Defines a consumer as any person who buys goods or hires/avails any services for a consideration paid or promised, including offline or online transactions through electronic means or by teleshopping or direct selling.

citations.title: Duties of E-Commerce Entities & Grievance Redressal Mechanism
citations.description: Every e-commerce entity shall establish an adequate grievance redressal mechanism and appoint a Grievance Officer whose details are displayed on its platform. The officer must acknowledge receipt within 48 hours and redress the complaint within one month.

citations.title: Manner in which complaint shall be made and Procedure before District Commission
citations.description: A complaint in relation to any goods sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or any service provided or agreed to be provided may be filed with a District Commission by the consumer, including online through the e-Daakhil portal.
